questions.stem: A substance has a high melting point and conducts electricity when dissolved in water but not when solid. What type of bonding does it have?
questions.explanation: This describes an ionic compound. Ionic compounds have high melting points, conduct when dissolved (ions free to move) but not when solid (ions fixed in lattice).

questions.stem: A substance is a gas at room temperature and does not conduct electricity. What type of structure does it most likely have?
questions.explanation: Simple molecular substances have weak intermolecular forces, giving them low boiling points (often gases at room temperature). They do not conduct electricity as they have no free charged particles.

questions.stem: A substance has a very high melting point, is very hard, and does not conduct electricity. What is it most likely?

options.text: A giant covalent substance like diamond

questions.explanation: Diamond (giant covalent) has a very high melting point, is very hard, and does not conduct electricity because all electrons are used in covalent bonds. Metals conduct, ionic compounds are brittle not hard.

questions.stem: Which type of substance conducts electricity in both solid and liquid states?
questions.explanation: Metals conduct electricity in both solid and liquid states because they have delocalised electrons that are free to move and carry charge regardless of the physical state.

questions.stem: Why does graphite have a high melting point but is also soft enough to use as a lubricant?

options.text: It has strong bonds within layers but weak forces between layers
It has weak bonds within layers but strong forces between layers
It has ionic bonds that break easily

questions.explanation: Graphite has strong covalent bonds within each layer (high melting point) but only weak intermolecular forces between layers. This allows layers to slide over each other, making it soft and useful as a lubricant.

questions.stem: Which property is common to both ionic compounds and metals?

options.text: They both have low melting points
They both have high melting points due to strong bonding throughout a giant structure
They are both gases at room temperature

questions.explanation: Both ionic compounds and metals have high melting points because they both form giant structures with strong bonds (electrostatic in ionic, metallic in metals) that require a lot of energy to break.

questions.stem: A substance melts at -183°C. What can you conclude about its bonding?

options.text: It is a metal with metallic bonding
It is a simple molecular substance with weak intermolecular forces

questions.explanation: A very low melting point indicates weak intermolecular forces between molecules, which is characteristic of a simple molecular substance. Giant structures (ionic, metallic, covalent) all have high melting points.
